page: Microsoft Azure M32ms is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by dedicated Intel Xeon 8280M processors clocked at 2.7 GHz, delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. For storage, the instance includes 1100 GB of local SSD capacity, with no integrated hardware accelerators.

The primary focus of the M32ms is its massive memory density, supplying 875.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 27.34 GB per vCPU. While the large uncached read and write memory bandwidths achieve 91.77 GB/sec and 37.23 GB/sec respectively, PassMark memory performance ranks in the bottom 25%. In computing tasks, the Intel Xeon 8280M architecture shows a clear contrast between single-core and parallel throughput. Benchmark metrics demonstrate bottom-tier single-threaded performance in Geekbench (896.0) and stress-ng (1038.69), as well as poor single-threaded compression throughput. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics such as PassMark CPU score (20875.13) and multi-threaded decompression align with mid-range tiers across the broader cloud landscape.

Given its hardware profile, the instance trades per-core single-threaded compute speed for extreme memory capacity. In transactional and operational testing, it sustained 20.43 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and average scores across database operations. The platform is well targeted for very large memory footprints that fit poorly on standard general-purpose servers, such as enterprise in-memory databases (SAP HANA, large Redis installations), relational database servers requiring vast buffer pools, and heavy in-memory data analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M32ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by Intel Xeon 8280M processors running at 2.7 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system offers 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache, an integrated 1100 GB local SSD, and no GPUs. With 875.0 GB of RAM, the instance delivers a high ratio of 27.34 GB of memory per core. Benchmark evaluations place multi-threaded throughput, database operations, and Redis caching in median performance categories, while single-core processing capabilities and single-threaded compression fall into lower percentiles. The server presents a distinct tradeoff favoring vast memory capacity over per-thread execution velocity. Consequently, the M32ms is specifically targeted at memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, memory-resident analytics, and high-capacity database caching systems.
